execution.solver: Explicit Python Newton/barrier/primal-dual implementation; SciPy LAPACK and SuperLU linear solves
execution.generator: NumPy PCG64; numeric seed and saved input arrays accompany each random instance

title: Barrier method on three SDP sizes
input_provenance: Random instances use NumPy PCG64, with saved arrays and seeds. They are method reproductions; MATLAB rand(state,...) uses v5uniform and randn(state,...) uses v5normal, whereas seed selects the v4 family. Equal integer seeds do not identify equal arrays. No exact MATLAB fixture was published in the checked companion sources; exact book-figure matching is not claimed.
notes: The textbook stops after relative gap reduction 10000 (LP) or 8000 (SDP); the companion instead requests absolute gaps 0.001 or 0.0001. This implementation follows the book relative-reduction experiment. For SDP it also retains the textbook random diagonal, unlike the companion zero-diagonal construction.
certificate_reconstruction: For each saved x, regenerate B, compute X=B+diag(x), W=X^-1, g=t-diag(W), H=W elementwise squared, dx=-H^-1 g, Z=(W-W diag(dx) W)/t. Saved objective/gap/eigenvalue/residual checks refer to this Z.
